author: KRISHNA CHAUDHARY
description: Navjot Singh, a 30-year-old trader, was shot dead inside his shop in Kumhariya Tah village on Saturday. CCTV footage captured two masked men arriving in a silver Maruti Alto before the attack. His father believes his stepsons conspired to kill him due to personal disputes over their mother's marriage. The police are currently searching for the two absconding suspects involved in the murder.
title: New Zealand-based stepsons shoot UP trader dead over mother’s 2nd marriage; CCTV emerges

author: SABI HUSSAIN
description: As the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Para Games approaches, India faces significant challenges concerning athlete selections and administrative delays. Recent disputes regarding the omission of key coaches from the para shooting contingent have created unrest among athletes. Delayed approvals for several disciplines have further complicated preparations, impacting kit distribution and athlete readiness. Athletes from badminton and table tennis confront last-minute issues just days before their events begin.
title: Asian Para Games: Coach row, court battles, clearance delays deepen chaos

author: LAIRENLAKPAM WARLI
description: Members of the Cockroach Janta Party gathered at Jantar Mantar carrying the national flag. They aimed to protest against the current government led by Narendramodi. Abhijeet Dipke reported on social media that certain individuals, including Ashutosh Ranka, were detained. The police intervened and took party members into custody during the protest. This situation highlights ongoing tensions between the party and government authorities over resistance movements.
title: CJP's Das, Ranka try to sneak into Jantar Mantar, detained by Delhi Police

author: NITIN NAIK
description: Ahead of India’s tour of New Zealand, NZC CEO Geoff Allott speaks to TOI about hosting the country’s biggest-ever series, record ticket sales, pitches, the IPL’s influence on Kiwi cricket and the enduring bond between the two nations.
title: IPL has helped develop Kiwi players and coaches: NZC chief Geoff Allott

author: SMITA MISHRA
description: Ishara is a pioneering restaurant chain that champions inclusivity by hiring individuals with hearing disabilities to amplify the dining experience. Founded by Prashant Issar, the flagship restaurant was designed to prioritize exceptional service alongside high-quality cuisine. By utilizing straightforward communication techniques, staff connect effortlessly with patrons. Comprehensive training programs empower employees with vital skills, fostering confidence and a strong sense of belonging as they thrive at Ishara.
title: Man's restaurant chain employs hundreds of hearing-impaired, spreads joy

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: In 2006, Star Trek star William Shatner’s kidney stone fetched $75,000 at auction. Shatner said the proceeds, along with another $25,000 raised by the Boston Legal cast, helped Habitat for Humanity build a home in Louisiana for a family of five. The unusual auction turned a personal medical episode into a charitable contribution with a lasting impact.
title: William Shatner sold his kidney stone for $75K to build a home

author: JYOTIRMOY HALDER
description: Sumit Nagal apologised to the Maia crowd and Portuguese player Henrique Rocha for making a “talking gesture” after his hard-fought first-round win at the Maia ATP Challenger. Nagal called it a heat-of-the-moment reaction and confirmed he had apologised personally to Rocha. The incident comes after India's disappointing Asian Games tennis campaign ended without a medal for the first time since 1986.
title: India No. 1 Nagal apologises to local Portuguese crowd for post-match gesture

author: TOI TECH DESK
description: Kroger Co intends to reduce its corporate workforce by around 3,000 positions over the next three years, as announced by CEO Greg Foran. This strategic move is geared towards streamlining operations and boosting efficiency. The restructuring is poised to enhance customer interactions while prioritizing investments in store staff. To further modernize operations, Kroger plans to incorporate cutting-edge technologies like artificial intelligence.
title: Kroger to lay off thousands, its largest cut in 143 years: what the CEO told staff

author: TNN
description: A devastating accident on Airport Road led to the arrest of four college students after their Mini Cooper collided with a scooter, resulting in the death of three people. Evidence suggests that the driver was under the influence at the time of the incident. The excise department is now looking into bars that supplied alcohol to the group, raising significant concerns over irresponsible drinking and driving.
title: Drinks, hotel, high speed: What we know about Kerala’s Mini Cooper crash; all held

author: SHIVANGHI PAYAL
description: India is projected to maintain a robust growth rate of 7% in both 2026 and 2027, bolstered by strong domestic demand and a thriving services sector, according to the International Monetary Fund. Positive revisions from the World Bank and OECD highlight resilience amid consumption patterns. However, challenges such as rising energy prices and geopolitical tensions could impact this trajectory, yet India's economic growth remains strong compared to other major nations.
title: India's economic story in fast lane, IMF projects 7% GDP growth for FY26 and FY27

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: In 2020, Alex Trebek and his wife, Jean, donated $500,000 to Hope of the Valley Rescue Mission. Two years later, their contribution had helped turn a shuttered, 60-year-old roller rink in Los Angeles into the 23,000-square-foot Trebek Center, a 107-bed homeless shelter designed to provide accommodation and mental health services to people experiencing homelessness.
title: Alex Trebek's $500K gift turned old rink into homeless shelter

author: TIMESOFINDIA.COM
description: At first, Kash Raju dismissed his worsening health as the result of stress and a busy family routine. However, persistent headaches and dizziness led him to seek medical assistance, where a CT scan disclosed a diagnosis of grade 4 astrocytoma, an aggressive brain cancer. He promptly had emergency surgery and began NHS treatment, with a prognosis suggesting he may have only 12 to 18 months left.
title: Brain cancer diagnosis: Man blamed headaches on stress before scan revealed tumour

author: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK
description: A tidy and hygienic kitchen is vital for preventing cockroach invasions. Using everyday ingredients like bay leaves and garlic powder can act as natural repellents. Cleaning with soapy water on a consistent basis helps eliminate food scraps that attract these pests. Additionally, storing food in sealed containers further reduces their interest. In cases of heavy infestations, seeking help from pest control experts could provide a more effective long-term fix.
title: 7 kitchen ingredients that keep cockroaches away

author: JYOTIRMOY HALDER
description: England batter Ollie Pope has withdrawn from the Afghanistan Premier League draft amid concerns over the Taliban’s treatment of women and girls. England cricket director Rob Key said participation was a personal moral decision, despite the ECB’s refusal to arrange bilateral series with Afghanistan. Former England batter Dawid Malan remains in the draft, highlighting the conflict between ethical concerns and players’ livelihoods.
title: Pope withdraws from Afghan league draft amid concerns over treatment of women

author: TANUJ LAKHINA
description: As Ahmedabad builds its case to host the 2036 Olympics, it faces competition from cities and countries with different advantages. From Munich’s existing venues and Qatar’s event-ready infrastructure to South Korea’s regional model, South Africa’s continental ambition, Istanbul’s Olympic experience and Hungary’s low-construction approach, each offers challenge, and lessons, for India.
title: 2036 Olympic hosts: Ahmedabad vs South Korea, Qatar, Munich, and 3 more

author: SHIVANGHI PAYAL
description: Oil prices fell on Tuesday after increasing nearly $2 a barrel the previous session. Concerns over energy supply disruptions from ongoing conflicts in the Middle East influenced market sentiment. Meanwhile, US sanctions on Russian fuel were temporarily lifted, allowing for additional diesel supply. OPEC revised its demand growth forecast downward, indicating overcapacity in the market.
title: Oil prices hold near $105 per barrel as Trump eases sanctions on Russian fuel

author: TOI TECH DESK
description: Tech giants and startups face an unprecedented shortage of computing power, causing internal strife over resources, particularly within Google and its competitors. Collaborative efforts have sprung up, such as the partnership between Anthropic and Elon Musk's xAI, aiming to enhance computing capabilities. As the quest for computational resources intensifies, the rental costs of advanced technology, like the Nvidia H100 chips, have soared, prompting firms to explore alternative global suppliers.
title: Silicon Valley’s “huge shortage”: Amodei calls Wang, Musk partners with a rival

author: ABHAY
description: A tragic altercation on a Delhi Metro train claimed the life of Pawan Sharma, the sole breadwinner of his family, on October 8. His death has left his wife and two children in deep sorrow. Authorities have taken action, arresting the individuals involved in the confrontation over reserved seating, and the case is currently under investigation for culpable homicide.
title: 'Mar gaya, mar gaya tera bhai': How row over metro seat turned deadly in Delhi

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: Matt and Amy Roloff bought their 16-acre Oregon farm for $185,000 in 1990, long before Little People, Big World brought the family fame. Now, 36 years later, their son Jacob and his wife, Isabel, face the possibility of leaving the property as Matt considers selling more of the land, leaving them devastated about their future.
title: Roloff's $185K farm now at center of family feud 36 years later

author: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK
description: The Kansas City Chiefs are set to bring in Justin Watson for a meeting at their training facility. As they look to enhance their receiving lineup amidst Tyreek Hill's uncertain situation, Watson's prior experience with their offensive system could offer critical support, even if he can't match Hill's explosive abilities. The team plans to assess both Watson's potential fit and Hill's status before finalizing any roster moves.
title: Tyreek Hill’s Chiefs reunion: Why are Kansas City eyeing their former star?

author: TOI WORLD DESK
description: An LS Lowry painting sold for over £805,000 at an auction after nearly a century in a family collection. Arthur Wallace, a British newspaper editor, purchased it for just £10 back in 1926. The painting, known as Going to the Mill, was created in 1925 and reflects Lowry's artistic focus on industrial life. The artwork highlights the transformation of its value from a lesser-known artist to a celebrated figure.
title: £10 Lowry painting kept 99 years sells for £805,200 at auction

author: NAVJEEVAN GOPAL
description: Punjab’s final electoral rolls have recorded a net decline of 13.60 lakh voters from the pre-SIR electorate, but the revision has drawn rare cross-party praise. Representatives of the AAP, Congress, BJP and SAD commended Chief Electoral Officer Anindita Mitra for transparency, consultation and addressing their concerns. Their endorsement comes amid protests against the Election Commission elsewhere, offering a striking contrast as Punjab’s voter list settles at just over 2.01 crore electors.
title: In a rare, all parties in Punjab hail CEC, 'transparent' SIR exercise
